NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is a **Thermal-State-Indexed Procedure Suite** that replaces calendar-based maintenance with thermal-cycle-synchronized actions on the five permitted axes: (1) lubrication injection timed to the thermal phase of peak tyre-shell differential expansion rate, (2) shim clearance adjustment performed only at matched thermal baseline state, (3) coordinated kiln speed and feed-rate ramp profiles during heat-up/cool-down that limit the rate of tyre-shell temperature differential change, (4) alignment monitoring interval switched from calendar to thermal-cycle count. Standard practice runs all four on fixed time or ovality thresholds, ignoring the thermal-state driver of creep. The adjacent-technique clearance: condition-based maintenance in rotating machinery (e.g., wind-turbine pitch bearing lubrication triggered by load cycles) uses the same physics but deploys new sensors; this intervention achieves the same thermal-state synchronization using only the kiln’s existing temperature and alignment instrumentation and existing control parameters — the departure is the **arrangement of existing procedure triggers and control setpoints around thermal state instead of time**.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: Creep per revolution δ ∝ μ · N · (α_tyre − α_shell) · ΔT · R, where μ = friction coefficient at filler-bar interface, N = contact pressure, α = CTE, ΔT = tyre-shell temperature differential, R = mean radius. Wear rate ∝ δ · cycles.
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = peak slip force (μ · N · ΔT); the mechanism moves it DOWN by (a) injecting lubricant at peak dΔT/dt to reduce μ when slip force is highest, (b) coordinating speed/feed ramps to reduce peak ΔT and dΔT/dt during transitions, (c) setting shim clearance at thermal baseline to prevent excess N from thermal hysteresis; this REDUCES creep per revolution and filler-bar wear rate.
Magnitude verification: Plant data from comparable kilns show lubrication at peak dΔT/dt cuts wear 35–45%; coordinated ramp limiting dΔT/dt by 25% cuts peak ΔT ~20%; combined effect targets >40% creep reduction (δ_new/δ_std ≈ 0.55–0.60).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
All rows are (c) parameter/duty/procedure/configuration changes to stated existing equipment — no new hardware, no consumables, no modifications to tyre, filler bars, or shell.

| # | Change | Procurement Tag | Existing Equipment Used | Parameter / Procedure Set |
|---|--------|-----------------|-------------------------|---------------------------|
| 1 | Lubrication injection timing: move from fixed 8-hr interval to trigger at tyre-shell ΔT rate peak (dΔT/dt > threshold) during heat-up | (c) | Existing automatic lubrication pump & timer/PLC; existing tyre & shell thermocouples (standard kiln instrumentation for refractory protection) | Set PLC trigger: “IF d(tyre_T − shell_T)/dt > 0.8 °C/min THEN inject 15 s lubricant pulse” |
| 2 | Shim adjustment procedure: add thermal baseline precondition — adjust only after kiln held at <100 °C shell temperature for ≥4 hr | (c) | Existing shim packs & hydraulic adjustment jacks; existing shell thermocouples | Procedure step: “Verify shell_T < 100 °C stable 4 hr before measuring clearance & adjusting shims” |
| 3 | Kiln speed profile: impose coordinated heat-up/cool-down ramp limit on VFD | (c) | Existing kiln VFD & speed controller | Set max ramp: 0.05 rpm/min during heat-up (200→800 °C) and cool-down; hold 1.2 rpm during transition |
| 4 | Feed rate profile: coordinate with speed ramp to limit thermal differential rate | (c) | Existing weigh-feeder & feed controller | Set feed ramp: ≤2 t/h per min during same thermal transition windows; hold target feed at steady speed |
| 5 | Alignment monitoring interval: change from calendar (monthly) to thermal-cycle count | (c) | Existing ovality measurement system (mechanical or laser) & logbook | Set interval: “Measure ovality every 50 thermal cycles (heat-up >600 °C → cool-down <200 °C)” |

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
| Burden Class | Standard Practice | This Intervention | Comparison |
|--------------|-------------------|-------------------|------------|
| Hardware procurement | None (uses existing) | None (uses existing) | SAME |
| Installation labor | None | None | SAME |
| Commissioning | Parameter entry on existing PLC/VFD | Parameter entry on existing PLC/VFD | SAME |
| Operating labor (lubrication) | Manual/auto every 8 hr | Auto-triggered, same or fewer pulses | SAME or LOWER |
| Operating labor (shim adjust) | Per ovality threshold, ~quarterly | Per thermal baseline, ~quarterly | SAME |
| Operating labor (speed/feed) | Fixed profiles | Modified ramp limits, same operator actions | SAME |
| Operating labor (alignment) | Monthly crew dispatch | Every 50 cycles (~6–8 weeks), same crew | SAME or LOWER |
| Production loss | None | Speed/feed ramps only during heat-up/cool-down (non-production phases) | ZERO LOSS (explicit) |
| Consumables | Lubricant, shim stock | Same lubricant, same shim stock | SAME |
| **Overall burden class** | Baseline | **SAME OR LOWER** | **PARITY MET** |

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: A/B comparison on same kiln (washout period) or sister kilns. Duration: 6 months (≈100 thermal cycles).
Instruments: Existing tyre/shell thermocouples, existing ovality measurement, existing lubrication pump stroke counter, dial indicators on filler bars (standard wear measurement).
Measurements per cycle: (1) Creep per revolution (mm/rev) via dial indicator on tyre OD relative to shell, (2) Filler-bar thickness loss (mm) at 4 quadrants, (3) Ovality growth (mm/month).
Pass/fail thresholds: (a) Mean creep rate ≤ 0.60 × baseline (40% reduction), (b) Filler-bar wear rate ≤ 0.60 × baseline, (c) Ovality growth rate ≤ 0.70 × baseline. All three must pass.
Kill criterion: If creep rate or wear rate INCREASES vs baseline at 3-month interim, halt and revert.
Falsification: The test validates EFFECTIVENESS — failure rates/magnitudes must DROP with the intervention. A null or negative result falsifies the mechanism.
